Module np.cincuentazo
Package np.cincuentazo.view

Class UiAnimations

java.lang.Object
np.cincuentazo.view.UiAnimations
public final class UiAnimations extends Object
Provides reusable micro-animation presets for JavaFX nodes in the Cincuentazo UI.

All methods are static and the class is final with a private constructor â€” it is a pure utility class with no instance state. Every animation is applied directly to the target Node's Node.translateYProperty(), Node.scaleXProperty()/ Node.scaleYProperty(), or Node.opacityProperty(), so callers need no knowledge of JavaFX animation internals.

Active-transition tracking

Each animated node stores its currently running ParallelTransition in its properties map under the key ACTIVE_TRANSITION_KEY. Before starting a new animation, the previous one is stopped so transitions never overlap and the node's transform state stays consistent.

SRP note

Keeping animation logic in this class means controllers and views never contain Timeline/Transition setup code â€” they call a single method and this class handles everything else.

  • Method Details

    • applyButtonMotion

      public static void applyButtonMotion(javafx.scene.Node node)
      Applies hover, press, and release micro-animations to a button-like node.

      Behaviour:

      • Mouse enter: node lifts slightly (translateY âˆ’1.5 px) and scales up to 102 %.
      • Mouse exit: node returns to its rest position.
      • Mouse pressed: node sinks (translateY +1.5 px) and scales down to 97 %, providing tactile press feedback.
      • Mouse released: node returns to the hover state if the cursor is still over it, or to rest otherwise.
      Parameters:
      node - the button or button-like node to animate; existing onMouseEntered/Exited/Pressed/Released handlers are replaced

      Parameters:

    • animateCardFromDeck

      public static void animateCardFromDeck(javafx.scene.Node deck, javafx.scene.Node card, Runnable onFinished)
      Animates a card flying from the deck pile to its final position in a player's hand, then invokes a completion callback.

      The card's position is initially overridden so it appears to sit on top of the deck (using scene-coordinate conversion), then a ParallelTransition moves, scales, and fades it back to its natural layout position over DEAL milliseconds.

      During the animation the card is set mouse-transparent to avoid accidental clicks, and the flag is cleared when the animation finishes.

      Parameters:
      deck - the deck pile node that acts as the animation's origin; its scene bounds are used to compute the start position
      card - the card node that will fly into the hand; must already be part of the scene graph (added to humanHand) before this method is called
      onFinished - callback invoked on the JavaFX Application Thread when the animation completes; may be null
